decision: made a git baseline of the v1 spike before touching code
why: the folder had no repo, so there was no way to diff or revert

decision: wrote the done predicate and module plan
why: a long autonomous run needs a falsifiable finish line

decision: dropped the android,web extractor args and switched to JSON progress lines
why: a test run showed those args force a 240p muxed file and worse audio; JSON progress gives percent and eta

decision: pickup and fade lengths walk back along the tapped beat grid, not one beat length times a count
why: second opinion: with tempo drift the pickup would start off the real beats

decision: linear gain ramps with cancel-and-hold, no setValueCurveAtTime
why: curves throw when automation overlaps; linear crossfades also suit two copies of the same recording

decision: commit planned transitions 3 s ahead and let a user pick revoke them; the outgoing voice is stopped only after the landing
why: a 250 ms lookahead starves when a background tab throttles timers to 1 s

decision: count-in lands on the pad clock: choose the pad bar first, then start the click one new-tempo bar earlier
why: second opinion: adding a new-tempo bar after a pad bar drifts off the pad grid

decision: sections keep the raw marked time and snap to a downbeat only when read
why: re-taps and fill renumber bars; overwriting the snapped time lets marks wander

decision: skipped per-set arrangements, meter changes, and a multi-slot voice queue beyond the committed timeline
why: no wireframe asks for them; the committed timeline already covers short sections

decision: added npm test over synthetic fixtures with known tempo, sections and keys
why: pure logic gets a check that fails if it breaks, before any screen depends on it

decision: kept plain Krumhansl-Kessler with a 90th-percentile gate; no major-key prior or bass weighting
why: real Way Maker recordings already read E in every 30 s window, so the extra tuning has nothing to fix yet
evidence: scratchpad/realkey.ts output: whole E, 17 of 18 windows E

decision: transport play state goes through a subscribe hook
why: e2e showed the Play button never re-rendered because React never heard about transport changes

decision: a mark that runs to the end of the file covers the last partial bar
why: e2e: Evening Test failed export with bars after 0:32 unmarked

decision: removed the synthesized pad and the retuned-pad fallback; pads only come from downloaded YouTube pads
why: user: not synthetic pads, use pads from YouTube

decision: Get all 12 keys queues the Worship Pads Spontaneous Vol. 4 album; any playlist link queues each track
why: user picked that album; one consistent sound across 12 keys

decision: e2e walks all 7 screens with real clicks and keys in headless Chrome against a fake yt-dlp
why: the done predicate needs a rerunnable check of every feature

decision: ran Get all 12 keys against real YouTube; 12 album pads imported with keys from titles, A pad loads as the 512 s stereo recording
why: user asked why they heard synthetic pads; proving the real album path end to end

decision: e2e Chrome runs with --mute-audio
why: the synthetic test tones were playing through the user's speakers during e2e runs

decision: compared all 7 screens to the PDF; fixed the seam preview layout, key cell look, TAP hint wrap, and the Download button state
why: lines overlapped labels and two controls looked different from the wireframe

decision: fixed position/pause recursion at the end of the buffer
why: second opinion found it; playing a song to its end on the Tap screen would overflow the stack
evidence: src/audio/engine.ts Transport.release; e2e 'playback stops cleanly at the end of the song'

decision: taps within 80 ms merge before the tempo estimate; gap fill is capped
why: second opinion: repeated Space at one paused spot made the typical gap 0 and the fill loop infinite
evidence: src/lib/songMap.ts buildGrid; test 'taps all at one time do not hang'

decision: pads stream through audio elements with a request ticket; cleanup runs on the audio clock
why: a decoded 8.5-minute pad is about 180 MB; stale async loads could leave a pad looping after Exit

decision: hold or pick during a song's ring-out lands on the next bar line, or ends the song
why: second opinion: the old path scheduled a landing in the past and cut into mid-section

decision: Perform keeps only the current and next song decoded
why: each decoded song is about 100 MB; a long set could exhaust a tablet

decision: kept: a pick made while the next section is already sounding applies after it lands
why: that section is the one playing when the pick takes effect, so its jump rule is the right one

decision: fixed 9 of 10 UI review findings: analysis overwrite, dead shortcuts after sliders, double Enter, stale audition, pad walk timing, empty-song bring-in, double album queue, LAN uuid crash and helper bind, migration rollback; debounced song writes
why: independent review of the screens and store found real user-facing bugs

decision: left two-tab duplicate imports as a ponytail note
why: one leader, one tab; the cost is a duplicate song, not lost data

decision: v1 last parts that end on the final downbeat run to the end of the song, in the db upgrade and the djw v1 reader
why: found while writing the migration e2e: the last bar was left unmarked

decision: correction to the 17:40 row: 17 of 18 thirty-second windows read E, not every window
why: the final review flagged the earlier wording as overstated

decision: added e2e checks for seam fade edits, a section-by-section .djw round trip, and the beat advancing in Perform
why: final review: those promised behaviors had no assertion

decision: built and tested from a clean copy of the tree with npm ci
why: done criteria 1 and 2 say from a clean checkout

decision: left open: a person tapping a real song, a real tablet or Safari, background-tab stalls over 3 s, the ring-out pick path, and two-tab imports
why: no automated check covers them and they need a human or hardware

decision: re-tapping replaces old taps only as new ones reach them; nothing clears the grid first
why: user: Re-tap the beat removed my sections. With no taps there are no bars, and sections are drawn on bars
evidence: src/screens/SongTap.tsx tap(); e2e 're-tap the beat keeps the sections'

decision: Backspace and an Undo button undo any edit on the Tap screen, from a per-visit history of 200
why: user: no way to start over or fix one section; Undo makes Start over safe without a confirm box

decision: left/right move by bar, up/down by section, 0 or Home to the start; back goes to the current start unless it was passed under 0.3 s ago
why: user asked for shortcuts to the start of the song, section and bar
evidence: e2e 'arrows step by section and bar'

decision: Select and Cut tools on the track strip; the strip left the seek slider, so clicking a section never moves the playhead
why: user asked for select (pickup, label and the like) and cut (nearest bar) tools when hovering sections
evidence: src/screens/SongTap.tsx Track, SectionInspector; e2e select and cut checks; docs/v2/screens/2b-tap-select.png, 2c-tap-cut.png

decision: a cut lands only on a bar strictly inside a section; the second half keeps the label and a hand-set key, and its pickup, fades and repeats start fresh
why: a cut on a section edge would do nothing, and the right half has no lead-in of its own
evidence: src/lib/songMap.ts cutBar, cutSection; npm test cut checks

decision: moving a section start stops a bar short of its neighbours
why: two sections on one bar collapse into one, so a nudge could silently delete a section
evidence: src/lib/songMap.ts moveSection; npm test and e2e clamp checks

decision: taps while playing use the heard playhead (position minus baseLatency and outputLatency) and the key event's timeStamp
why: position() ignored speaker latency, so every tap landed late, by 150 to 250 ms over Bluetooth
evidence: src/audio/engine.ts Transport.heard(); Chrome on this Mac reports 5 ms base plus 16 ms output

decision: a tap while playing snaps to the strongest nearby attack within 80 ms, weighted to the nearest; no snap without a clear attack (above a song-wide floor and 3x the local median)
why: user asked for taps that are just off to land on the beat; an attack-free pad intro should leave taps alone
evidence: scripts/test.ts snap checks; Way Maker live: median tap error 31 to 12 ms vs Beat This reference; in-app 8 taps 11-61 ms off saved within 10 ms

decision: Map the rest from the song replaces "Fill the rest from my taps": a tempo-state DP (madmom-style, beat length free to drift 4% a beat inside 0.8-1.25x the tapped beat) follows SuperFlux onsets out from the taps, forward, backward and across gaps
why: user wants to tap ~8 beats and have the app map the song; fill drew a straight line that drifted off live songs
evidence: Way Maker live (8:23, 68 BPM, live drift): F 0.977 mean over 6 seed points vs 0.15 for fill; studio take F 0.996; in-app run F 0.985 with no lost or extra beats

decision: mapped beats are stored as taps with auto: true instead of derived on read
why: the onsets need the decoded audio, which only the Tap screen has; Refine, Export and Perform read the grid without it

decision: onset finding runs in a worker after the Tap screen loads
why: about 1.1 s for an 8-minute song in Chrome; on the main thread it would freeze the screen, worse on a tablet
evidence: browser check: main thread never paused over 86 ms while the worker ran

decision: tuning: change cost 100 per unit of beat-length ratio, pull toward the tapped tempo 1 per unit of log ratio
why: grid search over 50/100/200 x 0/1/4 on two Way Maker recordings; 100 and 1 sit on a flat plateau, not a single best point
evidence: scratch eval vs Beat This (CPJKU) reference

decision: left open: rubato endings (Way Maker's last 15 s slows about 10%) and seeding in an unclear stretch (8 taps at 7:00 slipped one beat later on)
why: the follower holds tempo where attacks are weak; a person can re-tap a section
evidence: Way Maker eval misses at 479-482 s; seed 420 s same-count 0.90

decision: each fade pins its own start point before ramping
why: a linear ramp runs from the previous event, and cancelAndHoldAtTime adds none once the last ramp has finished, so the volume dropped at once when the next pass was scheduled
evidence: OfflineAudioContext render in Chrome: gain fell to 0.54 halfway through the section; e2e "the pass keeps full volume until its fade-out starts"

decision: fades follow an equal-power curve, drawn as 16 straight ramps
why: a linear crossfade of different audio dips 3 dB in the middle, which longer fades make audible
evidence: live check: summed power 0.998 to 1.000 across a 4-beat crossfade; unit test "a crossfade keeps its power steady"

decision: the fade-out end can move off the loop point (Section.fadeOutEndBeats, .djw fade_out_end, both optional)
why: asked for: a late end lets a crash or a held note ring over the next pass; an early end lets the old pass go quiet first
evidence: unit tests on fadeOutSpan; e2e "the old pass rings a beat past the loop point"

decision: going on to the next section keeps the same voice, with no fades
why: the recording is continuous there; two copies of the same audio crossfading made a swell, and early fade-outs edited for looping cut the singer's prompt
evidence: e2e "going on to the next section plays straight through"; live check: gain held at 1 across the boundary

decision: jumps between different sections line their fades up: match the fade-out (default), match the fade-in, or as edited
why: seams are edited for looping, so a jump from Chorus 2 (fades out 5 to 3 beats early) to Chorus 4 (fades in on the 1) left about 2 beats of silence
evidence: user report on Way Maker; unit tests on seamFades; live check: no gap when matched

decision: a seam that would leave silence can bring in a pad in the incoming section's key
why: the user asked for a pad under gaps; sections already know their keys, so no separate pad track is needed
evidence: live check: pad rose with the fade-out, held through the gap, and handed over to the new section

decision: a transition commits 3 s before its first fade starts, not before the new section's lead-in
why: a long fade-out (3 bars at 68 BPM is 10 s) started late and was squeezed

decision: Pause fades song and pads out over 3 bars, then suspends the audio clock; Resume fades back in over 2 bars; a Fade switch next to Pause (on by default, remembered) turns it off for the old instant pause
why: the user asked for a long, musical fade instead of an abrupt stop, and a gentle fade back in; suspending after the fade keeps every scheduled pass and seam in sync, and the set plays on under the fade so it resumes where it went quiet
evidence: e2e "Pause fades out instead of cutting", "the fade-out lasts 3 bars and ends silent", "Resume fades back in", "with Fade off, Pause stops at once"

decision: the pause fade follows even loudness (gain = progress^(1/0.6)), not the equal-power crossfade curve
why: heard loudness goes as gain^0.6, so this lowers it in a straight line: -4 dB a quarter of the way, -10 dB (half as loud) half way, -20 dB three quarters; equal power and a straight gain line hold loud and then drop away at the end, and a straight line in dB spends most of the fade nearly silent
evidence: unit tests "a pause fade lowers heard loudness in a straight line", "half way through a pause fade, it is 10 dB down"; second opinion agreed on the plan and flagged suspend races, handled by calling ctx.resume() first in resume()

decision: Perform pages to any song in the set (arrows, the set list, or Left/Right keys) while a song or pad plays; a section tapped there lands on the first bar line of what is playing that leaves room for its fades and a 1-bar count-in, and the Jumps setting lines up the two songs' fades; the set goes on from the song jumped to
why: the user wants to go back to an earlier song, or a section of it, mid-set; reusing the Jumps setting keeps song-to-song jumps sounding like section jumps; a second jump is refused until the first song lands, because two pending cross-song seams have no clean undo
evidence: e2e "it lands on a bar line of the song playing", "it lands on a bar line of Evening Test", "the old song has faded and stopped", "paging back from a pad shows the song that ended"; unit tests "a jump to another song never plays straight on", "nor counts as a loop"

decision: Start from any section (a song not yet started, and every section in "Start at" for the next song, now in both the song and pad views); Go to pad leaves the song (pad in on the next bar line over 2 bars while the song fades the same 2 bars), with the old behavior kept as "Pad under the song"; "Turn pad off" anywhere a pad sounds, and a song whose pad you turned off ends without one
why: the user asked to start anywhere, turn the pad off at will, and go to the pad or the next song whenever they want; Go to pad used to only layer the pad and leaving the song was hidden in More; a second opinion found the 8-bar kept-pad fade could not be turned off, ring-out Go to pad started mid-bar, and endSong could outlast the recording, all fixed
evidence: e2e "a song can start from any section", "and starts straight from it", "Go to pad brings the pad in as the song fades out", "the pad turns off between songs", "turning it off cuts its 8-bar fade to 2 bars", "Go to pad in the ring-out waits for the next bar line", "and ends when the recording does"

decision: removed the 1-bar count-in click, its setting, and the separate ear output it used; a song brought in now lands on the first bar line that leaves room for its fades
why: the user does not want count-in sounds while performing
evidence: e2e "with no count-in, it comes in on the first bar line it has room for"

decision: pick the pads for each gap between songs ("Change" on a live pad); picks are saved on the set keyed by the songs on both sides, so a reorder that changes the songs goes back to the suggested way in; Practice, the end of a song, and Go to pad open on the first picked pad in the library; Simple walks the picks; a pad under the song stays in its own key; Perform shows the picks in its set list, the Live pad box, and a "Your pads, from Sets" group; Simple counts steps so a key can come back later in the plan; with nothing picked, a missing end-key pad stays silent as before
why: the user asked to set or select the pads between songs in a set; second opinion agreed on the pair key and on keeping the pad under the song in the song key; the user did not see their picks in Perform; a second review found the repeated-key loop and the changed default
evidence: e2e 191 checks, including "practice opens on the first picked pad", "and on to a key that comes back later", "then stays on the last pad", "new songs around a gap go back to its way in"

decision: the pad under the song follows the sections: it starts in the key of the section playing, changes to each new section's key as that section lands (crossfade from the Pad-to-pad setting), and waits until the section can no longer be taken back; Perform shows 12 keys under the song to change it live on the next bar or beat, holding until the next section; a repeat pass keeps a tapped key
why: the user asked for the pad under a song to follow, or be changed for, each part of the song; it used to always play the key the song ends in
evidence: e2e "the pad under the song starts in the key of the section playing", "a key you tap changes the pad under the song", "and the next section brings its own key", "the pad changes key as the section lands"

decision: the suggested way in between songs follows docs/universal_key_modulation_strategy_guide.md: ride up the circle of 4ths into V to I when the next key is 1 to 3 steps up it, roll down the Anthem Roll (bVII IV I) when it is 1 or 2 steps down, and otherwise jump onto II V I, V I, or bVII IV I, whichever first chord keeps the most notes of the old key's chord (ties go II V I, then V I); Guided in Perform lists the guide's ways into the next key in place of the shared-chord pads, which stay in Advanced; a bVII pad is labelled bVII in the next key, not outside
why: the user asked to update every pad transition strategy to the new modulation guide; the old route picked a pad common to both keys before the V; second opinion agreed with the loop math and the worked examples and asked to keep the shared-chord pads reachable and to count a minor key's own chord
evidence: npm test: C to E plays C F# B E and G to E plays G B E as in the guide; D to E is now D A E (was D A B E)

decision: Space while stopped starts the song and adds no beat; e2e taps now happen while the song plays
why: a stopped tap went in unsnapped mid-grid and shifted every later bar, and Space is what most people press to resume

decision: Shift+Space or Beat 1 here while stopped marks or clears a 1 on the nearest beat, adding and moving none
why: there was no way to fix a wrong or missing 1 short of re-tapping

decision: a section mark past the last bar stays in the map and waits for its bar, shown as a count, not on the last bar
why: marks past the taps each renamed the one section on the last bar, so Verse, Chorus, Outro became one Outro
evidence: walk-through on the old code; src/lib/songMap.ts pastBars

decision: reaching the end of the recording runs the sections out to it
why: marks end lags the playhead by up to 0.5 s, which left a last bar unmarked on slow songs and failed export

decision: if the onset worker fails, Map the rest becomes Fill the rest from my taps
why: the button stayed disabled forever with only a tooltip, and tapping the whole song was the only way past the grid check
evidence: src/screens/SongTap.tsx; not run with a failing worker

decision: questions go through an in-page dialog (ui.tsx ask, askText), not window.confirm or window.prompt
why: tauri-plugin-dialog 2.7.3 replaces confirm with an async function, so if (confirm()) deletes at once; wry has no text input panel, so prompt returns null. Read from source, not seen in the app

decision: a map saved with an empty song name writes Untitled, and such a map opens
why: parseDjw refused the file it had just been given

decision: left bar-only cuts, no zoomable track editor, no Lock to BPM or drift graph, and no speaker-delay setting
why: bars are the data model and .djw format; the rest are replaced by the newer PDF and decisions above, or need real hardware to tune

decision: Calibrate taps: tap along to 16 clicks at 80 BPM, 4 to count in and 12 scored. The average offset, after leaving out outliers, is saved per device in localStorage and comes off new taps and section marks on top of the reported latency. This takes up the speaker-delay setting deferred above
why: outputLatency shipped in Safari 18.4 but no source says what it reports over Bluetooth or AirPlay, and it leaves out touch delay. Measuring through the same formula works whatever the browser reports
evidence: src/lib/tapCalibration.ts; npm test; e2e; second_opinion thread 9f3fd1f6 (1 of 3 models answered)
result: adopted; not tried on real Bluetooth, AirPlay or a phone

decision: the last click is higher, and a tap past it fails the check instead of saving a number
why: sound more than 600 ms late otherwise saves a believable small or negative offset, because every tap falls on some click
result: adopted; sound 600 to 1350 ms late plus a missed last click still saves a wrong number

decision: the check fails on drift as well as spread: the medians of the first and second half of the taps must sit within 70 ms, taken before outliers go
why: taps steadily drifting across 200 ms pass a 70 ms spread limit, and a sudden jump partway through gets left out as outliers, saving the wrong side

decision: the recalibrate hint watches reported latency moving 30 ms or more, and the screen always says to calibrate again after changing speakers or headphones. No devicechange listener
why: sources tie devicechange to capture permission and its behaviour in WKWebView is unverified. A native route listener in src-tauri would be the real fix

decision: the check uses the same TapPad as the song, so a Mac mouse click still counts at release
why: a pointerdown as the first gesture that unlocks audio in WKWebView can't be tested without an app build. Calibrate with the input you tap with
